author: Fiona McLoughlin
title: Woman discovers abandoned Oscars red carpet on Hollywood Walk of Fame - now it's decorating her home - NewsBreak
text:
By Fiona McLoughlin ,
8 hours ago A WOMAN on the hunt for a new rug discovered the Oscars red carpet was abandoned after the show Sunday night.
The carpet, walked on by celebrities like Teyana Taylor and Timothée Chalamet , now resides in the Hollywood production assistant’s apartment.
The red carpet was rolled out on Sunday at the Dolby Theater for the 98th annual Academy Awards (stock photo) Credit: Getty Paige Thalia searched for the red carpet after the Oscars and brought it to her Los Angeles apartment Credit: TikTok/hellopaigethalia Thalia found several remnants of the iconic carpet in a dumpster near the theater Credit: TikTok/hellopaigethalia Paige Thalia told The New York Times that she recently returned to Los Angeles after spending time traveling, and found decorating her new place was proving to be expensive.
The production assistant was on the hunt for a new, but cheap rug.
Before the Oscars kicked off, she noticed the red carpet was being installed outside the Dolby Theater in Los Angeles, California .
“I got the idea, when I was walking her down the red carpet, that I could maybe track that down after the awards,” she told the NYT.
Thalia said the idea actually formed almost a decade ago after she attended a taping of the Kelly Ripa talk show at the Dolby Theater.
After the taping, staff members handed out pieces of the red carpet to audience members, she revealed.
Thalia arrived at the theater Monday morning around 8:30am after the award ceremony concluded with One Battle After Another taking home the most awards.
Thalia initially thought her dreams had been crushed when she saw the carpet was already gone. But, she searched around hoping she could find the carpet nearby.

Just behind where Jimmy Kimmel Live! tapes, on a street near Dolby, the production assistant found a clean dumpster with the carpet inside.
She then asked a nearby security guard for permission to take her prized possession home.
“I said, ‘I have an insane question,’” she told the NYT. “‘Can I have some of that red carpet?’”
The security guard didn’t bat an eye, and pulled her own souvenir piece from her pocket.
Thalia then grabbed the biggest piece of carpet she could physically carry home and later unrolled the six-foot by eight-foot rug in her apartment.
Steve Olive, the owner of the company that provides the Oscars red carpet, said his rugs are made of recycled materials (stock photo) Credit: AFP Olive also revealed the red for the Oscars is an exclusive hue (stock photo) Credit: Getty Thalia said the rug was in “good shape,” and that she vacuumed it and trimmed it to make sure it fit into her space.
She said the rug did not appear to be designed to last, so she plans to add some trim to make it look more finished and to stop it from fraying any further.
Steve Olive, the owner of Event Carpet Pros, which has been the longtime carpet provider for the Oscars and other award shows, told The New York Times in 2025 that the shade of red for the Oscars carpet is an exclusive hue.
Olive also revealed that his carpets are made of recycled materials and are recycled after events.
Thalia documented her journey, sharing a video on TikTok , which gathered almost four million views as of Wednesday afternoon.
“These are huge,” she said of the dozens of rolled up carpets inside the dumpster. “I can’t take one that big … Is it insane to take a small piece?”
She told the New York Times she found some other treasures in her dumpster-diving adventures, including possible decor items and feathers from dresses.
“I did find a fake plant in it that must have come from some of the décor,” she said. “There were also some sequins and some feathers from dresses. I need to track down who might have been wearing those.”
